concerns.text: Task T012b mandates 'Geometry Calibration' (screen width, viewing distance) to calculate I-VT thresholds. The spec's FR-002 only requires a 'configurable threshold' and 'minimum fixation window'. The spec's Assumptions do not guarantee screen geometry metadata exists. This task introduces a hard dependency on metadata not required by the spec, creating a silent constraint violation where the pipeline fails if geometry is missing, whereas the spec only requires a configurable threshold.

Task T023b mandates running 'bootstrap samples' to verify '≥95% convergence rate' as a core implementation step. SC-002 defines the success metric as achieving convergence for '≥95% of bootstrap samples OR the full dataset'. The task forces the bootstrap execution path (which is computationally expensive and risks violating SC-004's 4-hour runtime limit) even when the 'full dataset' path would satisfy the spec. This is a semantic weakening of the success criterion by removing the 'OR' option.

Task T016 enforces a specific 'blink duration >200ms' exclusion rule. The spec's Edge Cases only define a threshold for '>50% missing frames' and explicitly forbid imputation. The 200ms blink threshold is an unverified scope addition not present in the spec or plan. This introduces a silent constraint drift where valid data might be discarded based on an arbitrary number not sanctioned by the research design.

Task T030 instructs to 'Delete intermediate figures after saving' to meet disk constraints. The Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) require that results be reproducible and traceable. Deleting intermediate figures (which may contain raw traces or un-aggregated data needed to verify the final plot's derivation) violates the 'Raw data is preserved unchanged; derivations are written to new filenames' hygiene rule and breaks the audit trail required for scientific reproducibility.
